mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Sunday, September 6, 2026. OpenAI announced it has met a goal set last fall to develop an automated research intern, described as a system capable of executing well-defined research tasks under human supervision. According to the company, this development is part of an effort to democratize understanding of frontier artificial intelligence by increasing transparency regarding how capable systems are built. OpenAI reports that its researchers are increasingly utilizing coding agents to contribute code and run experiments faster. While the company stated that automated research could enhance human welfare and help solve alignment and safety challenges, it emphasized that such progress does not guarantee a specific trajectory for future AI capabilities. OpenAI noted that it remains cautious, citing a recent incident involving Hugging Face that led the company to pause certain reinforcement learning training to conduct further security hardening and red-teaming. This shift reflects a growing emphasis within frontier labs on balancing rapid experimentation with the necessity of maintaining robust safety benchmarks, as more capable systems may become increasingly difficult to monitor. In the legal sector, two additional news organizations, The Seattle Times and Newsday, have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft. The publishers allege that the companies are using their copyrighted journalism to train generative artificial intelligence models without authorization. The lawsuit characterizes AI as a technology that consumes human-authored content to produce derivative imitations, potentially harming the viability of news organizations. This legal challenge is notable as it underscores rising industry anxiety regarding the sustainability of journalism in an era where AI models are trained on intellectual property, despite prior funding relationships between the defendants and some newsrooms. A Microsoft spokesperson stated the company was surprised by the filing but remains open to discussing potential solutions to the dispute. Meanwhile, a technical method known as ASCII smuggling is seeing increased use by spammers to evade email filters. The technique, which involves using specific Unicode tags to render text that is invisible to humans but readable by machines, was previously identified two years ago as a way to hide malicious prompts in AI attacks. Microsoft reported that it observed a significant increase in spam messages utilizing this method earlier this year, as the invisible tags allow spammers to obfuscate keywords that might otherwise trigger security detectors. By hiding instructions from human readers while ensuring they are parsed by machines, this method highlights the evolving challenge of filtering malicious content that exploits the way different software stacks interpret text. In infrastructure news, Amazon Web Services has released guidance on creating a Physical AI model factory, which integrates NVIDIA Cosmos 3 with its SageMaker HyperPod platform. The goal is to create a continuous pipeline for training robots and autonomous vehicles by generating synthetic data and evaluating models in a single, shared cluster. This approach helps mitigate the variability of GPU availability by allowing companies to commit capacity to a unified loop, thereby improving the useful pipeline progress per reserved GPU-hour. Separately, AWS introduced HyperPod InstantStart, a tool designed to help infrastructure teams automate the complex, multi-stage process of provisioning clusters for foundation model workloads using AI agents to manage workflows and dependencies. This tool aims to reduce the operational burden of managing Kubernetes and AWS resources by using agents to handle handoffs between dependent tasks. In an incident involving AI-assisted planning, three hikers were rescued from Mount Shasta in California after they reportedly relied on Google’s Gemini chatbot to plan their expedition. According to the Siskiyou County sheriff’s office, the hikers were advised by the AI to carry significantly less food and water than required for their journey.
